headline: Executives of major data center companies said at a Bloomberg forum in New Delhi that electricity and skilled workers, rather than chips or money, now limit how fast AI data centers can be built.
score_reason: Fresh, but these are executives' opinions at a forum and not new facts or decisions.
importance_line: Households may face slower, costlier AI services and higher power bills if building stalls, electricians and builders are in demand, and the views come from executives with their own business interests.
summary: Bloomberg reports that Abhijit Dubey, chief executive of NTT Data, called skilled labor the hidden bottleneck, saying a US electrician now earns about $200,000 and key equipment can take up to 42 weeks to source, while Connor Teskey, chief executive of Brookfield Asset Management, a major property and infrastructure investor, expects demand to outstrip supply through the end of the decade. Salil Parekh, chief executive of the Indian outsourcing firm Infosys, added that public backlash against the AI build-out in Western markets is a risk.
notes: Bloomberg original blocked; Bloomberg text read on Yahoo Finance.
